name: Stywe pap
summary: Stiff maize porridge: firm, smooth pap that holds its shape, made to scoop up stew, gravy and tomato-and-onion sauce at a braai.
about: Stywe pap — stiff porridge — is the firm maize-meal porridge eaten across South Africa, the everyday staple in many homes and the essential partner to braaivleis, stews and tomato-and-onion sauce. It is cooked thick enough to shape and is often eaten by hand.
steps: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pot, cast iron if you have it, over high heat.
Pour half the maize meal into the centre in a heap and do not stir. Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 8–10 minutes.
Uncover and stir hard with a wooden spoon, pressing the lumps against the side of the pot, for about 2 minutes, until smooth.
Add the rest of the maize meal a little at a time, stirring and cutting through the pap, until it is stiff and pulls away from the side of the pot. If it turns crumbly, add a splash of boiling water.
Cover and steam on the lowest heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring once halfway, until it no longer tastes raw and holds its shape.
Shape into rounds with a wet spoon or small bowl and serve hot with tomato-and-onion sauce, braaivleis or stew.
